newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine grain harvest forecast down to 27 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine grain harvest forecast down to 27 mln T.

text.p: Ukraine's grain harvest this year will be 27 million tonnes instead of 28 million tonnes predicted previously, the deputy prime minister said on Thursday.
Last year's harvest stood at 36.5 million tonnes.
"We are counting on getting 27 million tonnes of grain this year," Mykhailo Zubets told Reuters.
Zubets said 21.27 million tonnes had been gathered in the state sector, and that private farmers had raised their output this year to four million tonnes of grain from two million a year ago.
"This figure does not include the maize (corn) harvest, which, we think will be very good this year at two million tonnes," Zubets said.
Ukraine had predicted a harvest of 39 million tonnes at the beginning of the harvest season.
"Our forecasts for a good grain harvest this year were ruined by drought at the beginning of the summer," said Zubets.
The deputy prime minister said Ukraine would increase winter wheat sowing by one million hectares this year from 7.1 million hectares last year.
"Preparations for next year are going normally, and winter wheat sowing is proceeding normally," he said.
Zubets said rains during the last two weeks provided good moist conditions for the winter wheat.
"The weather forecast calls for warm conditions at the end of September and a warm October. We are counting on a much better harvest next year," he said.
He said government plans called for a 40 million tonne grain harvest next year.
"Beyond that the government has set a goal of an average of 50 million tonnes, with exports of 15 million tonnes," said Zubets.
